issues.description: The Person model's firstName field has different visibility in the template vs. the solution (and compared to the UML in the problem statement). The template's Person.java declares firstName as a private field with public getter/setter (matching the UML that shows '-' private fields), but the solution's Person.java declares the firstName field as public while still providing getters/setters. This discrepancy is a structural inconsistency across artifacts and may confuse students when they compare the template, UML/specification, and the reference solution (it also contradicts the intended encapsulation shown in the UML).
issues.suggested_fix: Ensure consistent visibility for Person.firstName across artifacts. Prefer preserving encapsulation shown in the UML and template by making firstName private in the solution (and keeping the public getter/setter). Alternatively, if making the field public was intentional, update the UML and template Person.java to reflect the public field and document the reason. The simplest fix to remove confusion: change 'public String firstName;' in the solution to 'private String firstName;'.
